stance_basis: research findings cited as factual background on earthquake recurrence intervals, no position on the project expressed
summary: Dr. Kerry Sieh of Caltech is referenced in the EIS as a researcher whose paleoseismic work on the San Andreas Fault provides useful data for assessing seismic risk to the proposed transit project. His Carbon-14 dating of nine major earthquakes extending back to the fourth century, yielding an average recurrence interval of 160 years, is cited to support the conclusion that a major earthquake on the San Andreas Fault is highly probable within the next 100 years. Dr. Sieh does not express a position on the project itself; his work is used purely as scientific background.
complaint_summary: Dr. Sieh's paleoseismic research on the San Andreas Fault near Palmdale is cited as providing Carbon-14 age-dated evidence of nine major earthquakes since the fourth century, with an average recurrence interval of 160 years, to support the assessment that a major earthquake is highly probable within the next 100 years.
